questions.stem: In the business life cycle, the seed stage is when:
options: the business has an established customer base, steady sales and loyal staff
sales are rising rapidly and the business is hiring more staff
sales are falling and the owners are considering closing the business
an idea is being developed and tested before the business begins trading
questions.explanation: The seed stage covers generating and testing a business idea, before the business is established. Rapid sales growth is the growth stage, and steady established sales describe maturity.

questions.stem: A Cairns kayak-tour business opened eight months ago. It has a small but growing group of customers, cash flow is tight, and the owner does most jobs herself. Which stage of the life cycle is it most likely in?
options: start-up
seed
maturity
decline
questions.explanation: A newly trading business building its first customers with limited cash and staff is in the start-up stage. In the seed stage the business has not yet begun trading.

questions.stem: A Toowoomba bakery chain has opened four new stores in two years, its sales are rising quickly, and it struggles to hire enough skilled bakers. Which life cycle stage best fits?
options: post-maturity
growth
start-up
maturity
questions.explanation: Rapid sales increases, expansion and pressure on staffing and systems are typical of the growth stage. In maturity, sales level off and competition for market share intensifies.

questions.stem: Which situation best describes a business in the maturity stage of the life cycle?
options: the business has just registered its name and is fitting out its first premises
sales growth has slowed, the market is crowded, and the business works to hold its share
the owner is researching whether customers want the product before launching it
sales are doubling each year as the business enters new regions for the first time
questions.explanation: In maturity, sales level off as the market becomes saturated and competitors fight for market share. Researching an untested idea is the seed stage, and fitting out first premises is start-up.

questions.stem: A not-for-profit or community-based organisation:
options: is owned by the government and run mainly to return dividends to the state treasury
is owned by shareholders who receive dividends from its profits
uses any surplus to pursue its purpose rather than distributing it to owners
is not allowed to earn more revenue than it spends in any year
questions.explanation: Not-for-profits can earn a surplus, but they reinvest it in their mission rather than paying it to owners. A business owned by government is a government-owned corporation or government business enterprise.

questions.stem: A Queensland government-owned corporation that generates electricity differs from a profit-based private company mainly because:
options: it is not required to cover its costs, because taxpayers pay all of its expenses
it cannot employ staff, so all of its work is done by public servants in departments
it is owned by the state government on behalf of the community, although it operates commercially
it is owned by private shareholders who can sell their shares on a stock exchange
questions.explanation: A government-owned corporation is run on commercial lines and aims to be efficient and profitable, but its shares are held by the government for the people of the state. It employs its own staff and is expected to cover its costs.

questions.stem: Which correctly orders the parts of strategic planning, from broadest to most specific?
options: mission, tactics, vision, strategies, objectives
objectives, vision, tactics, mission, strategies
vision, mission, objectives, strategies, tactics
tactics, strategies, objectives, mission, vision
questions.explanation: The vision sets the long-term aspiration and the mission states the business's purpose. Objectives give measurable targets, strategies are the broad plans to reach them, and tactics are the short-term actions that carry out each strategy.

questions.stem: A vision statement describes:
options: the dollar value of sales the business must reach this year
the legal structure under which the business is registered
what the business aspires to become in the long term
the specific steps staff will take this week to serve customers
questions.explanation: A vision is a broad, inspiring picture of the future the business wants to create. Specific weekly steps are tactics, and sales targets are objectives.

questions.stem: 'To provide affordable, healthy meals to busy Brisbane families, made from local produce.' This is best described as a:
options: mission statement, because it states the business's purpose and who it serves
tactic, because it describes a single short-term action for staff to complete
SMART objective, because it sets a measurable target and a deadline
SWOT analysis, because it lists the business's strengths and weaknesses
questions.explanation: A mission statement explains what the business does, for whom and how. It has no measurable target or timeframe, so it is not an objective, and it is not a single action.

questions.stem: A café sets the objective of increasing weekday sales by 15% within six months. Which is a tactic that supports this objective?
options: growing the business while caring for the community and the environment
offering a two-for-one coffee deal from 2 pm to 4 pm on weekdays next month
becoming the most loved café in Queensland within the next twenty years
increasing weekday sales by 15% within the next six months
questions.explanation: A tactic is a specific, short-term action that puts a strategy into practice. The twenty-year aspiration is a vision, the sales target is the objective itself, and the last option is a broad goal.

questions.stem: A new solar installer's goal is growth. Which objective best supports that goal?
options: open a second branch in Townsville within two years
keep the number of staff the same for the next five years
reduce the range of services offered to customers
pay all profits to the owners each year
questions.explanation: Growth means increasing the size of the business, such as more locations, sales or customers. Keeping staff numbers flat, cutting services and distributing all profit work against growth.

questions.stem: In a functional organisational structure, employees are grouped by:
options: specialist area, such as finance, marketing, human resources and operations
the product line or region that they work in, each with its own specialist staff
two managers at once, one for their function and one for their project
the year in which each employee first joined the business
questions.explanation: A functional structure groups staff by their specialised business function. Grouping by product or region is divisional, and reporting to two managers is a matrix structure.

questions.stem: A business with four separate product lines gives each line its own marketing, finance and operations staff. Which structure is this?
options: functional
matrix
flat
divisional
questions.explanation: A divisional structure organises the business into self-contained units by product, customer or region, each with its own functions. A functional structure would have one marketing department for all products.

questions.stem: In a matrix structure, an engineer reports to the engineering manager and also to the manager of the project she is working on. What is a likely problem?
options: staff cannot share their expertise across different projects or departments
the business has only one level of management
every decision must be approved by all shareholders
conflicting instructions from two managers can cause confusion
questions.explanation: Dual reporting lets expertise be shared across projects, but two managers may set competing priorities. A matrix structure is designed to share expertise, not prevent it.

questions.stem: A small Gold Coast design agency removes two layers of middle management so designers report directly to the owner. What is the most likely effect?
options: a more bureaucratic culture with stricter rules and procedures
faster communication and decisions, but a wider span of control for the owner
slower communication, because messages pass through more levels
fewer people reporting directly to the owner, so supervision becomes much easier
questions.explanation: A flatter structure shortens the chain of command, speeding communication and empowering staff, but the owner now supervises more people directly. More levels would slow communication, not speed it.

questions.stem: A software engineer at a Brisbane bank proposes a new mobile payments service and leads its development inside the bank, using the bank's staff and funds. Her role is best described as:
options: an intrapreneur
an entrepreneur
a company director
a franchisee
questions.explanation: Intrapreneurs innovate from inside an existing organisation, using its resources, while entrepreneurs create their own ventures and carry the financial risk themselves. Directors oversee management on behalf of shareholders.

questions.stem: In a public company, what is the main role of the board of directors?
options: to audit the company's financial statements as independent outsiders
to set strategic direction and oversee managers on behalf of shareholders
to serve customers and handle the day-to-day complaints that arrive at the front counter
to carry out daily operations such as rostering and ordering stock
questions.explanation: Directors are responsible for governance: setting strategy, appointing and monitoring senior management and acting in shareholders' interests. Day-to-day operations are run by managers, and audits are carried out by independent auditors.

questions.stem: How does the role of an owner-manager in a sole trader business differ from the role of a manager in a large public company?
options: the owner-manager answers to a board; the company manager answers to no one
the owner-manager cannot make any decisions; the company manager makes every decision alone
the owner-manager both owns and runs the business; the company manager is employed to run it
the owner-manager has limited liability; the company manager has unlimited liability
questions.explanation: In a small business the owner usually also manages it, carrying the risk and making most decisions. In a public company, managers are employees accountable to the board and shareholders.

questions.stem: A charismatic leader mainly influences staff through:
options: personal charm, confidence and the ability to inspire enthusiasm
strict rules, written procedures and a clear chain of command
rewards for meeting targets and penalties for missing them
adapting their style to each employee's level of readiness
questions.explanation: Charismatic leaders draw followers through their personality and energy. Strict rules describe bureaucratic leadership, rewards and penalties describe transactional leadership, and adapting to readiness is situational.

questions.stem: A bank branch manager insists that every loan follows the written procedures exactly and that all decisions pass through the proper levels of approval. Which leadership style is this?
options: coaching
bureaucratic
transformational
authentic
questions.explanation: Bureaucratic leaders rely on rules, procedures and hierarchy, which suits highly regulated tasks where consistency matters. Transformational leaders focus on inspiring change rather than following set procedures.

questions.stem: A sales manager pays a bonus to staff who exceed their monthly targets and gives warnings to those who fall well short. Which leadership style is this?
options: transformational
transactional
charismatic
mentoring
questions.explanation: Transactional leadership is an exchange: rewards for meeting agreed targets and consequences for missing them. Transformational leaders instead seek to inspire staff to go beyond their own interests for a shared vision.

questions.stem: A new chief executive inspires staff with a vision of becoming Australia's most sustainable retailer and encourages them to challenge old ways of working. Which leadership style is this?
options: situational
transformational
bureaucratic
transactional
questions.explanation: Transformational leaders motivate staff through a compelling vision and intellectual stimulation, driving major change. Bureaucratic and transactional styles focus on rules and exchanges rather than inspiring change.

questions.stem: A team leader meets each staff member weekly to set development goals, give feedback and help them build skills for future roles. Which leadership style is this?
options: bureaucratic
charismatic
transactional
coaching
questions.explanation: Coaching leaders focus on developing individuals' skills and long-term performance through guidance and feedback. Transactional leaders focus on rewards for current results rather than development.

questions.stem: A leader openly shares her values, admits mistakes and makes decisions consistent with what she says she believes. Which leadership style does this best describe?
options: bureaucratic
transactional
charismatic
authentic
questions.explanation: Authentic leaders are self-aware, transparent and guided by genuine values, which builds trust. Charismatic leaders rely on personal appeal, which is not the same as transparency and consistency.

questions.stem: A manager gives detailed instructions to a new apprentice but leaves an experienced, confident technician to decide how to complete his work. Which leadership style is the manager using?
options: situational, because the style changes with each employee's readiness
bureaucratic, because each employee is following the business's set written procedures
transactional, because both employees are rewarded for results
charismatic, because the manager inspires both employees equally
questions.explanation: Situational leadership matches the amount of direction and support to the follower's competence and commitment, so the apprentice gets close direction and the technician is given autonomy. Nothing in the scenario involves rules, rewards or personal charm.

questions.stem: An experienced senior partner at a law firm meets a junior lawyer every month for two years, sharing career advice and professional insights. How does this mentoring differ from coaching?
options: mentoring is a longer-term relationship focused on overall career development
mentoring focuses only on short-term sales targets, with bonuses paid for meeting each one
mentoring requires the junior lawyer to follow written procedures exactly
mentoring is used only in emergencies when there is no time to consult
questions.explanation: Mentoring is usually a long-term relationship in which an experienced person guides a less experienced one's broader career, while coaching focuses on specific skills and performance. Bonuses for targets describe transactional leadership.

questions.stem: Which business criterion measures how well a business uses its resources to produce its output?
options: efficiency
effectiveness
competitiveness
stakeholder satisfaction
questions.explanation: Efficiency is about using resources such as time, money and materials with minimal waste. Effectiveness is about whether objectives are achieved, competitiveness about performing against rivals, and stakeholder satisfaction about meeting stakeholders' needs.

questions.stem: A business set an objective of 1,000 online orders in March and received 1,050. Using the business criteria, this result shows that the business was:
options: inefficient, because it went over its target
effective, because it achieved its objective
efficient, because it used the fewest resources possible
competitive, because it outperformed all of its rivals
questions.explanation: Effectiveness is the extent to which objectives are achieved. Meeting the target says nothing about how many resources were used or how rivals performed.

questions.stem: Two options for a new Mackay gym are compared: Option A cuts membership fees to win customers from two rivals; Option B adds childcare that members have asked for. Which statement correctly applies the business criteria?
options: Option A mainly targets efficiency, while Option B mainly targets competitiveness against its two rivals
both options mainly target efficiency, because they both change the use of resources
Option A mainly targets effectiveness, while Option B mainly targets efficiency
Option A mainly targets competitiveness, while Option B mainly targets stakeholder satisfaction
questions.explanation: Cutting prices to take customers from rivals is about competitiveness, and responding to members' requests is about stakeholder satisfaction. A full evaluation would also consider each option's effect on efficiency and effectiveness.

questions.stem: Which key business function is mainly responsible for acquiring, developing and keeping the business's staff?
options: marketing
finance
human resources
operations
questions.explanation: Human resources manages the employment cycle, from recruitment and training to retention and separation. Operations turns inputs into goods and services, marketing deals with customers, and finance manages money.

questions.stem: A business introduces cloud accounting software that shows its cash position in real time. Which key business function benefits most directly?
options: human resources, because staff can now be recruited through social media
marketing, because the software creates advertising campaigns automatically
operations, because the software controls the production line machinery
finance, because managers can monitor cash flow and make timely decisions
questions.explanation: Real-time financial data helps the finance function manage cash, budgets and reporting. Technology supports every function, but this software's main benefit is financial information.

questions.stem: A SWOT analysis for a Sunshine Coast surf school lists 'highly qualified instructors' as a strength and 'growing numbers of international tourists' as an opportunity. Which strategy best uses the relationship between them?
options: list the instructors as an opportunity, since they could leave the business
market premium lessons to international visitors, highlighting the instructors' qualifications
reduce the number of instructors to cut costs, as international tourists do not value qualifications
close the school during the tourist season to avoid crowded beaches
questions.explanation: Strategic planning uses internal strengths to take advantage of external opportunities. Cutting the strength or avoiding the opportunity wastes both, and staff are internal, so they belong under strengths or weaknesses, not opportunities.

questions.stem: Why is an analytical tool such as SWOT useful in strategic planning?
options: it organises internal and external information so managers can set realistic objectives and strategies
it calculates the exact profit the business will make in each of the next five years of trading
it replaces the need for a mission statement and a vision statement
it guarantees that the chosen strategy will succeed whatever competitors do
questions.explanation: SWOT summarises strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats so managers can match strategies to the business's situation. It does not forecast exact profits or guarantee success.
